basis: Immunodeficiency; bronchiectasis (2/3) follows infections, while Crohn/ulcerative colitis (1/3 each) are separate diagnoses. Diarrhea alone does not establish direct bowel damage.

decisions.pulmonary: none: bronchiectasis in 2/3 is a separately diagnosed consequence of recurrent infections; direct immune-mediated lung injury lacks a frequency.
decisions.gastrointestinal: none: Crohn disease and ulcerative colitis (1/3 each) are separately diagnosed diseases; diarrhea in 3/3 alone does not demonstrate direct bowel damage.

basis: Mitochondrial metabolic disease; cerebellar atrophy/developmental impairment and sensorineural hearing loss each affect 2/2. Pectus alone lacks functional damage; aspiration pneumonia is secondary.

decisions.musculoskeletal: none: pectus carinatum in 2/2 is a structural finding without demonstrated functional damage; hypotonia does not establish direct muscle disease.

basis: Rickettsial infection with a defining necrotic cutaneous inoculation eschar; this is direct skin injury. Transient rash and headache add no axes.

decisions.dermatologic: primary: the characteristic necrotic inoculation eschar is a defining cutaneous lesion explicitly included in the disease definition.

basis: Distal motor neuron or axon degeneration defines this neuropathy; muscle wasting and weakness result from denervation rather than direct muscle pathology.

decisions.musculoskeletal: none: common muscle wasting reflects denervation from motor neuron or axon disease, without evidence of direct skeletal muscle pathology.

basis: Metabolic bone disorder defined by excessive osteoclastic resorption and disordered remodeling. Hearing loss, nerve compression and cardiac failure are minority complications.

decisions.metabolic_endocrine: primary: abnormal bone turnover defines this metabolic bone disorder, explicitly supported by its metabolic bone disorder parent.

basis: Inherited susceptibility defined specifically by myeloid blood-cell malignancy. The primary axis classifies the predisposition; it does not assert existing leukemia or marrow damage.

decisions.haematologic: primary: the susceptibility concept is defined by myeloid blood-cell neoplasia. Future leukemia is not counted as involved organ damage.

basis: Immune arthritis with defining urethritis; keratoderma/nail dystrophy 80-99%. Oral ulcers 80-99%, colitis and iritis 30-79% omitted at cap; conjunctivitis transient.

decisions.renal: primary: urethritis is explicitly part of the defining classic triad, qualifying despite its occasional HPO frequency of 5-29%.
decisions.gastrointestinal: none at cap: oral ulceration (80-99%) and colitis (30-79%) qualify, but extensive skin/nail disease is retained alongside the three primary axes.
decisions.ocular: none at cap: iritis (30-79%) qualifies but is omitted in favor of more frequent skin/nail disease; transient conjunctivitis adds no axis.
decisions.dermatologic: involved: keratoderma and dystrophic nails represent direct skin/nail disease annotated in 80-99%, retained preferentially under the four-axis cap.

basis: Lysosomal storage with defining skeletal and corneal disease; valvular disease occurs in 80-99%. Neurologic abnormalities annotated 80-99% are omitted at the four-axis cap.

decisions.ocular: primary: characteristic corneal clouding is a defining feature of Scheie syndrome, supported by the eye-disorder ancestry; ocular disease is not merely a complication.

basis: Sellar CNS tumor arising from Rathke pouch remnants in the pituitary region; direct optic pathway compression causes visual acuity or field loss in 30-79%, excluding treatment effects.

decisions.metabolic_endocrine: primary: this Rathke pouch-derived sellar tumor occupies the pituitary region; pituitary neoplasm and hypopituitarism are annotated in 80-99%.

basis: Cerebellar disease and axonal neuropathy define SCA43. Pectus (4/7) lacks demonstrated functional damage; pes cavus and amyotrophy (30-79%) do not establish direct musculoskeletal disease.

decisions.musculoskeletal: none: pectus in 4/7 lacks demonstrated functional damage; pes cavus and amyotrophy (30-79%) accompany neuropathy without established direct bone or muscle injury.
